explanation: Try each root position and compare the full candidate tree there. An empty target is a subtree; a nonempty target cannot match an empty root.
timeComplexity: O(1+n(m+1)) safe worst-case bound for n root-tree nodes and m target nodes: each candidate may compare m nodes, and candidate traversal costs O(n). An empty target returns immediately.
spaceComplexity: O(h + t) recursion space for the two tree heights. Candidate-root recursion and equality recursion share at most the sum of their tree heights in active frames.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A nonempty target is a subtree exactly when it equals the whole tree rooted at some node. Trying each candidate root and applying structural equality covers every such position. The explicit empty-target rule supplies the base case, and no node values or links need modification.
walkthrough: In tree [8,4,10,2,6,9,12], inspect the subtree rooted at 4. Its children are exactly 2 and 6, matching target [4,2,6] in both values and structure. Return true.
edgeCases: An empty target is a subtree of any tree.
A nonempty target cannot occur in an empty root tree.
Matching values with extra or missing children is insufficient.
